limitations: Register combines the original static audit with completed atlas and source-layout additions. Browser-only uploaded/custom images and a newer unsaved live campaign were not independently inspected.

Ready to reuse is limited to the stated purpose: geographic orientation or explicitly prepared new map variant. It does not certify exact source geometry, physical table calibration or flawless image registration.

World and all six regional annotated sheets were rendered and visually reviewed. Generated terrain can drift from official reference coordinates: Neverwinter river-mouth and Mount Hotenow peak alignment are documented examples. Plates are not seamless tiles.

Twenty Phandelver SVG variants received manual source-map and room-key comparison, full-render inspection and targeted topology/opening checks. Natural contours, clutter, vegetation and some furnishings are simplified. The 620 checks are regression evidence, not proof of pixel-perfect tracing.

Book audit covers meaningful regions, settlements, venues and destinations; it was not a page-by-page inspection of every complete book. Unplaced minor venues, dungeon rooms, individual Ten-Towns settlements and Loudwater have no invented regional pins.
Personal PDFs remain local read-only references. Scan offsets differ, particularly Dragon Heist; source references distinguish visual verification from text extraction and inference.

The register, private atlas data, DM annotated SVGs, source scans and topology companion remain private. Public projection includes only reviewed artwork, approved broad geography and discovery-filtered records; Presentation blocks flagged composites.

Existing scene IDs, selected original art and saved fog/tokens/notes are retained. A source variant is an opt-in new scene with blank fog, not an automatic migration. Staging an unkeyed map exposes its full ordinary layout.

No miles or travel durations are calculated from image coordinates. Only directly sourced distances are numeric; other distances remain unknown. Walking Tower is a roaming area, Broken Star an approach area; proposed Nine placements do not establish discovery.
Arrival-routing follow-up is tracked separately until its integration and preservation checks complete.

bookLimitations: This is a candidate register, not a claim to every proper noun or every printed map label in the three full PDFs.

No PDF page was newly visually verified during this subtask. All evidence comes from existing extracts and selected direct pypdf text extraction; exact wording and page limitations are stated per row.
No map coordinates, boundaries, travel lines, or surface-to-Underdark alignments have been verified. Broad contexts are suitable for matching against independently checked maps.
SCAG describes its own era and frequently uses in-world narrators; hidden places and uncertain rumors remain qualified. Later setting events must not be silently folded into this source snapshot.

Canonical published identity and a book-suggested placement are different. Optional Tales adaptations and seasonal Dragon Heist access locations require campaign choices before fixed pins are presented as established geography.
Street-level positions of several named venues, mobile ships, and sites whose location the book withholds remain deliberately unresolved.
The eight additional Ten-Towns settlements are not separately established by SCAG pp. 98–99 text reviewed here; only Bryn Shander and Targos are named. Other sources or maps may establish the rest.
SCAG minor venues and map-only labels, Dragon Heist poster-map street names and every generic encounter template, and Tales individual dungeon rooms are outside this register.

contractRoutes.label: A Map Worth Paying For
contractRoutes.route: Portal well → 1 → ordinary south exit bending west → 2a → steps down into 2b → northern stairs/corridor → eastern branch toward 6a. The northern one-way secret door in area 1 is not an ordinary usable entrance from the well side. Check the actual map for bends and door positions.

contractRoutes.label: The Missing Instrument
contractRoutes.route: Entrywell 1 → actual 2a/2b approach → southern stairs and corridor → 25a tool pile and excavation mouth. Area 25a→25b uses the published 5-foot-wide, 5-foot-high rough tunnel. Stop at 25a unless the party chooses and can support the extra survey.

contractRoutes.label: Terms of Passage
contractRoutes.route: Primary travel lane is the established 1→2a→2b→25a; it does not cross area 6 or require an Undertaker toll. If the party chooses a supervised rendezvous at the previously observed 6a threshold, negotiate that northern side trip separately along the mapped approach. It is a meeting point, not a presumed refuge or resting place. Contact at Worg’s Eye is an optional, separately prepared extension: 25a → low tunnel 25b → its west door → unkeyed western passage → 24b south door → 24a north exit → the southern area-23 corridor → 23a/23b, resolving the actual gate approach and guards. Area 23c opens off that corridor; it is not the route into 23b. The 26b closet opens from 26a and is not on this western passage. The cube starts in 26c on the separate southern branch, not automatically on this route. Do not route negotiators through the lethal mirrors in 21 as a shortcut.
